stem: About what share of India's passenger traffic is carried by roads every year?
options: About 40 per cent
About 70 per cent
About 85 per cent
About 95 per cent
explanation: Correct option: (C). Roads carry about 85 per cent of passenger and 70 per cent of freight traffic every year. 70 per cent is the freight share, 40 per cent is the share of road traffic carried by National Highways, and 95 per cent is the share of foreign trade by volume moving through ocean routes.

stem: National Highways form only about 2 per cent of India's total road length but carry about 40 per cent of road traffic. What does this show?
options: Traffic per kilometre is much heavier on National Highways than elsewhere
Most of India's road traffic moves on rural roads rather than on highways
National Highways are built mainly for defence movement, not general traffic
National Highways are longer in total than all the State Highways together
explanation: Correct option: (A). A road class carrying 40 per cent of traffic on 2 per cent of the length carries about 20 times its proportional share (40 / 2 = 20), so traffic density on National Highways is very high. Rural roads form about 80 per cent of the length but do not carry most traffic; National Highways serve inter-state traffic as well as defence; and Table 7.1 shows State Highways (1,76,818 km) are longer than National Highways (1,36,440 km).

stem: A trader wants to send goods by road from Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat with the least travel time. Which highway project is planned to serve this route most directly?
options: North-South Corridor, since it links India's northern and southern ends
East-West Corridor, since it is planned to link Silchar with Porbandar
Golden Quadrilateral, since it joins the four biggest metro cities
Grand Trunk Road, since it runs from Amritsar to Kolkata in the east

stem: Why is the density of rural roads very low in hilly, plateau and forested areas of India?
options: The Central Government does not allow roads in these regions
Roads in these regions are counted as National Highways instead
These regions are already well served by inland waterways
Rugged terrain makes building roads there difficult and costly

stem: The Atal Tunnel (9.02 km) was built by the BRO in the Pir Panjal range at about 3,000 m above mean sea level. Which statement best explains its importance?
options: It links Lahaul-Spiti with Manali all year, ending the winter cut-off
It is an international highway linking India to a neighbouring country
It replaces the high Chandigarh-Manali-Leh road with a lowland route
It allows the valley to be served by Pawan Hans helicopters in winter
explanation: Correct option: (A). Before the tunnel, Lahaul-Spiti was cut off for about six months a year by heavy snowfall; the tunnel connects it to Manali throughout the year. It lies wholly inside India, so it is not an international highway; it does not replace the high-altitude Chandigarh-Manali-Leh road; and it is a road tunnel, not a helicopter service.

stem: In 2019-20 India had 63,950 km of broad gauge, 2,402 km of metre gauge and 1,604 km of narrow gauge track. About what share of the network was broad gauge?

About 84 per cent
About 94 per cent
About 99 per cent

stem: About 95 per cent of India's foreign trade by volume but only about 70 per cent by value moves through ocean routes. What can be inferred from this?
options: Goods sent by other modes, like air, have high value per unit weight
Sea routes carry mostly light and costly goods like medicines and gems
Most of India's foreign trade by value moves along inland waterways
Ocean routes are used only for trade and not for travel to the islands
explanation: Correct option: (A). If ocean routes carry 95 per cent of the volume but only 70 per cent of the value, the remaining 5 per cent of volume sent by other modes accounts for about 30 per cent of the value, so it must be costly per unit weight. Sea routes suit heavy, bulky goods; inland waterways carry only about 1 per cent of transport; and ocean routes are also used for travel between the islands and the mainland.

Manage air traffic and aeronautical services in Indian air space

stem: A medical team must reach a flood-hit remote hill area in the north-eastern states within hours. Which mode suits best, and why?
options: Inland waterway, as it is the cheapest mode for heavy and bulky cargo
Pipeline, as it is the most efficient mode over very long distances
Narrow gauge railway, as it is generally confined to hilly regions
Helicopter service such as Pawan Hans, fast and suited to hilly areas
explanation: Correct option: (D). Air transport is the fastest mode and copes with difficult terrain; Pawan Hans helicopters operate in hilly areas of the north-east. Waterways are cheap but slow, pipelines carry liquids, gases and slurry, not people, and railway density is low in the hill and north-eastern states, so a narrow gauge line is unlikely to reach the area quickly.

stem: A state wants to map changes in its forest cover over several years to manage natural resources. Which satellite system best suits this need?
options: INSAT, as it is a multi-purpose system for telecommunication
PSLV, as it is the satellite that sends images to ground stations
Radio broadcasting, as it reaches almost every household quickly
IRS, as it collects data in many spectral bands for resources
explanation: Correct option: (D). The Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) satellites collect data in several spectral bands and transmit it to ground stations, which makes them very useful in managing natural resources. INSAT mainly serves telecommunication and meteorological observation, PSLV is a launch vehicle rather than a satellite, and radio is a broadcasting medium that cannot map forests.
